<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.23.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.23.0): pnpm 12.23

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.22.0...v12.23.0)

This release adds `pnpm edit`, `pnpm catalog migrate`, and `pnpm link --hard`, and moves deprecation warnings into the install summary. Platform variants are removed, so packages that publish them need to move to `optionalDependencies`. It also carries security fixes: pnpm no longer reads `otp` from config files, and it sends registry credentials only over HTTPS.

##### Minor Changes

##### Packing and publishing

- Removed platform variants. A package version has one archive again.

  pnpm no longer reads `publishConfig.variants` or the `variant` field of `package.json`. `pnpm pack --variant` and the `--upload-variant`, `--variant-integrity` and `--no-variants` options of `pnpm publish` are gone. pnpr no longer accepts variant archives with a version or serves them at `<name>@<version>/variants/<tag>`.

  To ship builds for several platforms, publish each as its own package and list them in `optionalDependencies`. A frozen install of a lockfile that records the variants of a registry package fails with `ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE`. Run `pnpm install` to resolve the lockfile again.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now fail if a package that is not private lists a private workspace package in `dependencies`. A private package is never published, so the published package could not be installed. `devDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, and bundled dependencies are still allowed [#​2321](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2321).

- `pnpm publish` now supports `--new-version <version>`, which sets the version in `package.json` before publishing. With `--recursive`, every selected workspace package is set to the new version [#​2168](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2168).

- `pnpm pack --json` now reports the `package.json` that goes into the tarball, with `publishConfig` and the other publish-time changes applied. Run `pnpm pack --dry-run --json` to preview it without writing a tarball. A dry run still runs `prepack` and `prepare`, unless `--ignore-scripts` is passed.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now add a workspace-root `COPYING` file to a workspace package that has no license file. A `COPYING` file at the package root now counts as the package's license, so the workspace-root `LICENSE` is no longer added next to it.

- Added the `versioning.includePrivatePackages` setting. Set it to `false` to leave private packages out of `pnpm change` [#​13813](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13813).

##### Managing dependencies

- Added the `pnpm edit` command to open an installed package directory in an editor.

- Added `pnpm catalog migrate`, which moves dependency specifiers into the default catalog and replaces them in the workspace projects' `package.json` files with `catalog:`. A dependency moves only when every project declares it with the same specifier. The command lists the dependencies it leaves unchanged [#​7072](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7072).

- Added a `--hard` option to `pnpm link`. With `--hard`, pnpm saves the linked package with the `file:` protocol, so its files are hard linked into `node_modules` and its dependencies and peer dependencies resolve from your project. `pnpm unlink` removes these links too [#​9895](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9895).

- `pnpm remove` now accepts glob patterns and `!` exclusions in dependency selectors, such as `pnpm remove "eslint-*" "!eslint-plugin-import"` [#​13546](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13546).

- When pnpm updates a `package.json5`, it now changes only the values that changed. Comments, quotes, number formats, and layout elsewhere in the file stay as written. New keys and strings use the quote style of the file.

- `nodeLinker` accepts object settings for isolated and hoisted installs. Linker-specific hoisting options can be configured alongside the selected linker.

##### Updating dependencies

- `pnpm update --latest <pkg>` now moves the override that pins the named dependency [#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8701). `pnpm update --interactive --latest` does the same for every selected dependency. An override keeps its own range shape: a pin on an exact version lands on the new exact version, and `^` stays `^`. When pnpm cannot update the governing override automatically, the update prints a warning naming it.

- `pnpm update` now accepts `--tag <tag>`. The flag updates the matched dependencies to the version behind the given dist-tag and rewrites the ranges in `package.json`, the way `--latest` updates to the `latest` tag. It also works with `--interactive` and with global updates [#​3534](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/3534).

- With `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`, `pnpm update --interactive` shows a `Trust` column with the trust evidence of each offered registry dependency [#​8889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8889). The list also offers only versions the trust policy accepts, so it matches what the update installs.

- `pnpm update --interactive --long` shows the homepage or repository URL of each package. The URL column is hidden without `--long`.

##### Release age and build settings

- Added the `referenceTime` setting. `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicyIgnoreAfter` count back from this RFC 3339 time, both when pnpm resolves versions and when it verifies a lockfile. Set it in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or with `PNPM_CONFIG_REFERENCE_TIME`.

- Added the `--minimum-release-age` and `--minimum-release-age-exclude` options to `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, `pnpm update`, and `pnpm dlx`. They set `minimumReleaseAge` and `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` for a single run without editing a config file [#​11224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11224).

- `pnpm audit --fix` accepts `--no-add-release-age-exclusions`, which applies the fixes without adding entries to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`.

- `--allow-build` now accepts a comma-separated list of packages, so `pnpm add foo bar --allow-build=foo,bar` is the same as passing `--allow-build=foo --allow-build=bar` [#​9560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9560).

##### Install output

- Deprecation warnings moved into the install summary and only name the packages the install added. A deprecated dependency added by the install is marked `deprecated` on its summary line, with the version that is not deprecated when there is one. Deprecated subdependencies the install added are listed right after the summary. Deprecated packages that were already installed are reported as one count, such as `3 deprecated packages are still installed`.

- In a workspace, the install summary now lists the direct dependency changes of every project, not only of the project pnpm runs in. Each change is listed once, followed by the projects that made it, unless only the current project did. A project's first install lists only deprecated or outdated dependencies and the ones the command added [#​6481](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6481).

- `pnpm install` now warns when an entry in `overrides` matches no dependency, in a single line such as `2 overrides matched no dependency: foo, parent>child`. Only the overrides declared in the workspace are checked. Overrides added by a config dependency or an `updateConfig` hook are not. Set `warnUnusedOverrides: false` to turn the warning off [#​10315](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10315).

- `pnpm install` now shows lockfile verification progress while the supply-chain check runs. The final pass or failure line reports how many entries were checked.

##### Setup and diagnostics

- `pnpm doctor` now checks the environment that lifecycle scripts run in. It lists the `node` executables on `PATH` and warns about broken ones. It reports the shell that runs scripts. A new check runs a package's executable from a script, both in a temporary project and in the current project. If that script fails, the report includes the error and, outside Windows, a trace of the executable's shim that shows how it looked up and started `node` [#​16308](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16308).

- `pnpm self-update`, `pnpm setup`, and the "Install method" check of `pnpm doctor` now warn when another `pnpm` on `PATH` would run in place of the one pnpm installed. The warning names that copy. If pnpm recognizes how it was installed (npm, Homebrew, Corepack, Volta, or Scoop), the warning also gives the command that removes it.

- Set `PNPM_CONFIG_HOME` to choose the directory containing `config.yaml` and `auth.ini`. Global configuration commands read and write files in this directory. A non-empty value takes precedence over `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and the platform defaults.

- pnpm now provides a prebuilt binary for Linux on LoongArch (loong64) with glibc.

- A failed `devEngines.runtime` or `engines.runtime` check now reports the reason in its error code. A runtime that is not installed fails with `ERR_PNPM_RUNTIME_NOT_FOUND`. A runtime entry without a version range fails with `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_RUNTIME_VERSION_RANGE`, and one with an invalid range fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_RUNTIME_VERSION_RANGE`. An installed version that does not satisfy the range still fails with `ERR_PNPM_BAD_RUNTIME_VERSION`.

- `pnpm view <pkg>` now prints the registry it read the metadata from at the end of the summary [#​11394](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/11394).

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- `otp` is no longer read from any config file. Pass `--otp` on the command line, or set `PNPM_CONFIG_OTP`. A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or a global `config.yaml` that carries `otp` is ignored, with a warning naming those two channels. `pnpm config set otp` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_SET_NOT_A_FILE_SETTING`.

  This closes a way to leak a secret. A repository could write `otp: ${NPM_TOKEN}` beside its own `registry:`, and `pnpm publish` sent that environment variable to the registry the same file named, in the `npm-otp` header of its first request [#​13542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13542).

- pnpm now sends registry credentials only over HTTPS or loopback HTTP, both for tarball downloads and for requests to `pnprServer`. Tarball and package metadata requests respect registry credential paths on redirects. A failed tarball request can no longer pin its redirect destination in the lockfile.

- `pnpm install` now rejects local filesystem dependencies (`file:`, `link:`, and path-based `workspace:` specifiers) declared by non-local packages with `ERR_PNPM_LOCAL_SUBDEP_NOT_ALLOWED`. Relative `file:` dependencies inside a package's own archive and local dependencies configured by the workspace through `overrides`, `packageExtensions`, or `.pnpmfile.cjs` continue to work. Lockfile verification also rejects unauthorized local directory, tarball, and link entries on non-importer snapshots.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now enforce `blockExoticSubdeps` against entries in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Before, pnpm accepted a lockfile with git or tarball URL subdependencies and installed those packages even with `blockExoticSubdeps: true`.

- `pnpm install` with `pnprServer` now rejects registry-keyed lockfile entries whose resolution uses a non-registry source with `ERR_PNPM_RESOLUTION_SHAPE_MISMATCH`. The `pnpr` lockfile verification and resolution endpoints enforce the same check before accepting or caching a lockfile.

- `pnpm dlx`, `pnx`, and `pnpm create` now ignore local configuration in the working directory. This covers `.pnpmfile.cjs` hooks, proxy and TLS settings in the project `.npmrc`, and execution, layout, and resolution settings in a local `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, including `pnpmfile`, `globalPnpmfile`, `configDependencies`, `scriptShell`, `cacheDir`, `storeDir`, and `ignoreScripts`. Settings from the user's global `config.yaml`, such as `blockExoticSubdeps`, `cacheDir`, and `storeDir`, remain active.

- Global commands (`--global`, `-g`) no longer load `.pnpmfile.cjs`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or `.npmrc` from the current working directory. `pnpm why -g` now inspects globally installed packages.

- `pnpm config get` refuses to print protected auth settings. `pnpm config list` hides TLS private keys and inline proxy credentials. `pnpm config set --global tokenHelper` writes to `auth.ini`, and setting a project-level `tokenHelper` fails.

  TLS file paths in `.npmrc` and `auth.ini` resolve relative to the file that declares them. Project `.npmrc` files skip TLS file paths containing environment variables.

- When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, it now handles registry credentials the way pnpm does:

  - Credentials configured for a registry path, such as `//registry.example.com/org-a/npm/:_authToken`, are sent only to that path. They were sent to any path on the same host.
  - It reads the registry and credentials from the global `auth.ini`, where `pnpm login` writes them, and from the `_auth` setting of the global `config.yaml`.
  - A `${NPM_TOKEN?}` placeholder in `.npmrc` expands to the variable. It expanded to an empty value, so the download was sent without credentials.

- Matching a glob that repeats a wildcard, such as `+(*)z` in the workspace `packages` patterns, no longer hangs on long paths. The bundled picomatch is patched for a [security advisory](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now reject `publishConfig.directory` values that use an absolute path or `..` segments outside the package directory.

- The `pnpm` binary no longer depends on `chrono`, which RustSec reports as unmaintained in RUSTSEC-2026-0543.

##### Installing packages

- `pnpm install` now adds a new workspace package that has no dependencies to the `importers` of `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​18189](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18189).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore` on, `require.extensions` hooks run again for `require()` calls from a module compiled from a string, such as the module Next.js uses to load `next.config.ts`. A required `.ts` file skipped the registered TypeScript hook. A required `.json` file was parsed as JavaScript [#​18261](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18261).

- On Windows, when the project is on a network share, `pnpm install` now links dependencies in `node_modules` with the kind of link that can be opened on that share. It tries a junction first and a symlink second. If neither can be opened, the install fails with advice.

- On Windows, concurrent installs that link the same dependency no longer leave an `.ignored_<name>` entry next to the link in the global virtual store.

- `pnpm install` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a `file:` dependency that is not a workspace project uses a `catalog:` specifier. Injected workspace projects still resolve their `catalog:` dependencies.

- A `link:` or relative-path dependency of a local directory dependency now resolves from that directory. In any other package, such as a local tarball, it resolves from the lockfile directory. Both used to resolve from the importing project's directory [pnpm/tasks#319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/319).

  Two workspace projects that declare the same injected relative-path dependency, such as `../child`, no longer share the directory the first one resolved.

- `pnpm install` now links a workspace package for a `workspace:` range that combines `^`, `~`, or `*` with other ranges, such as `workspace:^ || ^2.0.0`.

- Fixed `pnpm install` keeping a runtime binary for the previous platform after a change to `supportedArchitectures` with the global virtual store disabled.

- The `nodeVersion` setting no longer changes the global virtual store directory names or the side-effects cache keys. These follow the Node.js runtime that pnpm installs for the project, then the `node` on `PATH`. `pnpm licenses` and `pnpm store status` now find packages that an install with `nodeVersion` placed in the global virtual store.

- Fixed package maps resolving workspace and linked packages to the wrong directory when a path contains `#`, `?`, or `%`.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report a `catalog:` peer of an injected workspace package as unmet when the installed version matches the catalog entry [#​10279](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10279).

- The peer dependency check now reads the version of an injected workspace package from its `package.json`. `pnpm install` with `strictPeerDependencies: true` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report such a peer as unmet with a `file:` version.

- With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now reports missing peers of linked workspace packages, as `pnpm peers check` does.

- `peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions` now accepts a parent version range that contains `>`, such as `"foo@>=1.0.0>bar": "1"`.

- Fixed `nodeLinker: hoisted` installs in a workspace where the directory of one project is inside the directory of another. A dependency of the inner project could resolve to the version in the outer project's `node_modules`. pnpm now keeps the inner project's dependency in its own `node_modules` when the outer project holds another version.

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, pnpm now finds the agent skills of a dependency whose directory is shared with another peer variant of the same package version.

- `pnpm install` with `pnprServer` set now handles more workspace settings:

  - It applies `injectWorkspacePackages`, `dedupeInjectedDeps`, `ignoredOptionalDependencies`, and `dependenciesMeta`. Projects that use them no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` or `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH`.
  - `pnpm install --update-checksums` refreshes the integrity checksums in the lockfile.
  - It enforces `minimumReleaseAgeStrict` and adds fallback versions to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` when strict mode is off.
  - It resolves locally when the project declares `file:`, `link:`, or local path dependencies, or when `blockExoticSubdeps` is `false`. `pnpr` also rejects local filesystem dependency specifiers on `/-/pnpr/v0/resolve`.

- When an overrides entry requests a version that does not exist on the registry, `pnpm install` now names that override entry in the error. If the entry's selector has a version range, such as `foo@^1`, the error also shows the latest published version in that range.

- `pnpm add` run from a workspace package directory that has no `package.json` yet now suggests creating one with `pnpm init` [#​11345](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11345).

- The install summary now shows "(X is available)" after a direct dependency whose `latest` version on the registry is newer than the one installed. The note appears when the install resolved that dependency against registry metadata.

- Approving the `minimumReleaseAge` prompt no longer reprints the list of packages it just showed. pnpm now confirms with one line that says how many entries it added to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​15377](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15377).

- pnpm now prints a warning that explains why it has to remove and recreate a modules directory.

- `pnpm install` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` no longer hangs or runs out of memory in large workspaces whose packages are installed with many different sets of peer dependencies.

- Sped up `pnpm install` on macOS for packages installed with several sets of peer dependencies. pnpm now clones every peer variant of a package from one cached copy of its files.

- Sped up linking bins in large workspaces. pnpm now reuses a workspace package's `package.json` across the projects that depend on it when linking their bins.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer waits for a Node.js version check it does not use before it exits. With Homebrew's Node.js, a frozen install with nothing to do can be about 3x faster.

- Resolving a remote tarball uses the download response directly, saving a request.

- pnpm in StackBlitz WebContainers sends HTTP response bodies and subprocess output to its engine as raw bytes. A 64 KiB chunk no longer becomes a 234 KB message [pnpm/tasks#63](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/63).

##### Lockfile

- Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_NEXT_LOCKFILE_NOT_REPRESENTABLE` under `lockfile.format: v13` when a peer dependency is provided by an aliased package and another alias installs the package that has the peer's name [#​18198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18198).

- Fixed writing v13 lockfiles when a package has an ordinary npm alias of one of its direct or transitive peers [#​18274](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18274).

- Fixed conversion to the v13 lockfile format when a hashed peer suffix includes a workspace link and the package installs its own copy of another declared peer [#​18288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18288).

- `pnpm install` now converts an existing lockfile when you change `lockfile.format`, even when all dependencies are already installed. With `lockfile.format: v13`, an install that updates a v9 lockfile without resolving, for example after a dependency is removed, now writes the v13 format.

- A lockfile in the experimental `v13` format now always records `autoDedupe`, `dedupeInjectedDeps`, `dedupePeerDependents` and `linkWorkspacePackages`, as `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings` does for the `v9` format. After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with `autoDedupe`, `pnpm run` no longer starts another install. Run `pnpm install` once to record the settings in a `v13` lockfile written by an earlier version, since `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on it [#​16583](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16583).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now checks the dependencies of local directory dependencies against the lockfile more closely. It fails when the `injected` setting of such a dependency no longer matches the lockfile [pnpm/tasks#319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/319). It accepts a plain-range dependency that `linkWorkspacePackages: deep` linked to a workspace project.

- Frozen installs now detect changes to catalog entries used only by peer dependencies of local directory packages.

- Frozen installs now restore links declared through catalogs when `excludeLinksFromLockfile` is enabled.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now revalidates registry metadata when verifying a locked tarball whose version is missing from the cached package listing.

- During dependency filtering in commands such as `pnpm install --prod --frozen-lockfile`, pnpm now recovers hashed peers in v9 lockfiles only when a binding can affect which dependencies are kept [#​18276](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18276).

- Fixed `pnpm install --lockfile-only` fetching a locked transitive Git dependency when an unrelated dependency changes [#​18217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18217).

- Fixed `pnpm fetch` failing when a Docker build copies the lockfile before the workspace configuration or pnpmfile.

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` now quotes strings that look like numbers, such as `+.5`, so they are read back as strings.

##### Build approvals

- `pnpm approve-builds --all` and `pnpm approve --all` no longer approve a package whose build is denied with `false` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

- A `<pkg>@<version>: false` entry in `allowBuilds` or `permissions` now also blocks `<pkg>@<version>` from a named registry, including when `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` is set.

- `pnpm add --allow-build` now records its decision under `permissions` when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a `permissions` setting. Before, a `--allow-build=!<pkg>` denial went to `allowBuilds` and was overridden by an existing `permissions.<pkg>.build: true`.

- `pnpm approve-builds` now requires the exact selector shown by `pnpm ignored-builds` for a dependency a bare package name cannot identify (a `file:`, git, or tarball artifact)

Issues.Title: Angular SSR can render itself until the server runs out of memory when `Host` carries the server's port
Issues.Body:
### Description


During SSR, a relative `HttpClient` URL is resolved against the URL of the request being rendered, [port included](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/53ef99a543e037b64c596e9c3e147cb365062cea/packages/platform-server/src/http.ts#L82-L93). The Node adapter builds that URL from `Host` as it arrived, and `allowedHosts` checks the host name:

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/bdda8bbf1bfb80aaffdb1121e58c7dd97b5a2e4f/packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/validation.ts#L134-L154

So with `example.test` allowed, a request with `Host: example.test:4000`, 4000 being the port Node listens on, passes the check, and the page's relative requests go to the SSR server itself instead of the reverse proxy in front of it. The SSR server doesn't serve the API path and the app's `**` route matches it, so `AngularServerApp.handle()` renders it like any other page (it only skips `/favicon.ico` and the DevTools file):

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/bdda8bbf1bfb80aaffdb1121e58c7dd97b5a2e4f/packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts#L156-L198

That render runs the same root component, which sends the same request, which is rendered again. Nothing marks a request as coming from a render and nothing limits the depth, so one request grows a chain of renders until the heap runs out. The API never gets a request from it.

The app is `ng new --ssr` on 22.3.0. Its root component shows the site's settings, which a service gets from the API:

```ts
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class SiteConfig {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);

  get() {
    return this.http.get<{ title: string }>('/api/config');
  }
}
```

Every route renders on the server (`RenderMode.Server` on `**`, as in the SSR guide), unknown paths get a not-found page, `allowedHosts` is `["example.test"]`, and `server.ts` is the generated one. The proxy sends `/api/` to the API and the rest to Node.

These proxies pass the client's port on to Node in `Host`, and `localhost` in `allowedHosts` leads back to Node wherever the proxy is. One request each, on 22.3.0 unless the row says otherwise, in a 1 GB container (Node picks a 560 MB heap):

| Setup | The request | Process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nginx with Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 `proxy_params` (`Host $http_host`, also in PM2's nginx guide) | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 14.1 to 15.4 s |
| nginx with Ubuntu 26.04 `proxy_params` (`Host $host$is_request_port$request_port`, also in Debian testing) | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 14.7 s |
| Nginx Proxy Manager, a proxy host as its UI makes it | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 14.3 s |
| Apache with `ProxyPreserveHost On`, which it needs here (with `Off`, Angular answers 400) | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 15.3 s |
| Caddy, `reverse_proxy` with its defaults | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 14.2 s |
| Traefik with its defaults | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 12.7 s |
| HAProxy with its defaults, 22.3.0 or 21.2.31 as generated | `Host: example.test:4000` | exits after 13.4 to 15.1 s |
| `localhost` also allowed, nginx with `Host $http_host` on the same or another machine | `Host: localhost:4000` | exits after 15.6 to 15.8 s |
| `localhost` also allowed, Kubernetes with ingress-nginx or Traefik and an Ingress with no host | `Host: localhost:4000` | the pod's container exits after 13.0 to 13.5 s |

The `proxy_params` rows are the distro's own nginx package with a site that only does `include proxy_params;`. nginx needs some `Host` line in front of Angular: without one it sends `127.0.0.1:4000` and Angular answers every request with 400. The site's name resolves to the machine that runs Node, as on a VPS with the proxy next to Node. In Kubernetes it points at the load balancer, so there it takes `localhost`. `*` in `allowedHosts` works like `localhost` with any name.

It isn't tied to `HttpClient` in a service: `httpResource` in the root component ends the process after 14.7 s, a resolver on a layout route after 12.5 s.

Proxy headers do the same where Angular trusts them. `X-Forwarded-Host: example.test:4000` ends the process after 13.7 to 14.9 s on 20.3.43 and 21.2.31 as generated, and after 14.6 to 15.2 s on 22.3.0 after `ng update`, even with a `Host $host` line as in the NGINX reverse proxy guide. 20.3 and 21.2 trust `x-forwarded-host` and `x-forwarded-proto` unless `trustProxyHeaders` is set:

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/52184525966cf1a034359f902b53b5875a9dadc9/packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/validation.ts#L255-L257

22 trusts neither, and the v22 migration adds both to every server file that creates `AngularNodeAppEngine`:

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/bdda8bbf1bfb80aaffdb1121e58c7dd97b5a2e4f/packages/schematics/angular/migrations/trust-proxy-headers/migration.ts#L80-L83

With `trustProxyHeaders: true`, `X-Forwarded-Port` and, on 22, `Forwarded` do the same through Debian's `proxy_params`, which set `Host $host`.

`allowedHosts`, added in angular/angular-cli#32516, compares host names, so a port in `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Host` passes. That's known: angular/angular-cli#33128 proposed checking it and was closed with "Validation is handled by the user when using the `trustProxyHeaders` configuration". This issue doesn't ask to change that. It's about what follows when the port is the SSR server's own: the render requests itself, again and again. No row of the table depends on a trusted proxy header.

### Minimal Reproduction

https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-ssr-self-render-loop-lab

```sh
cd docker
docker compose up -d --build site nginx
node ../tools/attack.mjs "Host: example.test:4000"
docker compose ps -a site
```

```text
visitor   GET /              200, site: from-api, 42 ms
visitor   GET /no/such/page  200, site: from-api, 15 ms
attack    GET / with Host: example.test:4000
visitors  12 answered (median 17 ms, max 89 ms), then 502, site: -, 2258 ms at 15.3 s
attack    502, site: -, 15264 ms after 15.3 s
visitor   GET /              ECONNRESET
```

`docker compose ps -a site` shows `Exited (134)`. The README has the commands for the other rows, the other versions and the other places of the request.


### Exception or Error

```text
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
----- Native stack trace -----

 1: 0x9434f0  [node]
 2: 0x75f7fa node::OOMErrorHandler(char const*, v8::OOMDetails const&) [node]
```

### Your Environment

```text
@angular/ssr      22.3.0, 21.2.31, 20.3.43
@angular/core     22.3.0, 21.2.26, 20.3.35
@angular/build    22.3.0, 21.2.31, 20.3.43
Express           5.3.0
Node.js           24.22.3 in Docker (node:24-slim)
nginx             1.24.0 from Ubuntu 24.04 (also 1.18.0 and 1.28.3 from Ubuntu, 1.26.3 from Debian 13, 1.30.7 from nginx.org)
Proxies           Nginx Proxy Manager 2.17.1, Apache 2.4.71, Caddy 2.11.9, Traefik 3.8.0, HAProxy 3.4.8
Kubernetes        k3s 1.34.1 with ingress-nginx 1.15.1 or Traefik 3.3.6
```

### Anything else relevant?


The relative URL interceptor already sees every `HttpClient` request a render sends, so it could mark them, and `AngularServerApp.handle()` could decline to render a request that carries the mark. That would end the loop whatever puts the SSR server's own address in the URL, without touching how `allowedHosts` treats ports.

Until then, each of these stops it in the lab: `proxy_set_header Host $host;` in nginx, not trusting proxy headers that the proxy passes on from the client, and keeping `localhost` out of `allowedHosts`.

I think this is a DoS vulnerability according to the [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/SECURITY.md), which says:

> DoS attacks which waste server resources significantly beyond the cost of the attacker's request may be security issues.

Here a single request, with a port the client writes in `Host`, ends the process in about 15 seconds , which cause a OOM
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Angular SSR can render itself until the server runs out of memory when `Host` carries the server's port" (#72223)

Issues.Title: build: add Bazel g3_mode flag and acceptance_g3 test target
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Adds a Bazel `--//tools/bazel:g3_mode` flag and `g3_test` transition wrapper so `g3-only` / `3p-only` code paths and type overloads can be compiled and tested directly in this repo without waiting for a g3 sync.

### How it works
- **In-memory transform in `rules_angular`** (`tools/bazel/patches/rules_angular_g3_mode.patch`): When `--ngG3Mode` is passed, the worker wraps `fs.readFile` to apply the markers documented in `contributing-docs/google-markers.md` and uses a fresh `FileCache` so 3P and g3 compilations never collide. Because files stay at their original paths, there is no `root_dir` / relative-import rewriting and zero overhead for normal 3P builds.
- **Bazel flag & transition** (`tools/bazel/BUILD.bazel`, `tools/bazel/g3_mode.bzl`, `tools/defaults.bzl`): `g3_test` transitions `--//tools/bazel:g3_mode=true` across the full dependency graph so `@angular/core`, `@angular/core/testing`, and specs all build consistently in g3 mode.
- **`*_g3_spec.ts` convention** (`packages/core/test/acceptance/BUILD.bazel`): `acceptance_g3` runs `**/*_g3_spec.ts` (excluded from 3P `acceptance_lib`, with `acceptance_g3_lib` and `acceptance_g3_raw` tagged `manual`). Includes a smoke test in `g3_mode_g3_spec.ts` verifying `g3-only` / `3p-only` markers, `OnPush` default in g3, and `3p-only` API stripping.

### Verification
- `pnpm bazel test //packages/core/test/acceptance:acceptance //packages/core/test/acceptance:acceptance_g3` — both pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "build: add Bazel g3_mode flag and acceptance_g3 test target" (#72216)

Issues.Title: Angular 22.3.0 installation fails with ERESOLVE due to incompatible OXC WASM and EMNAPI peer dependencies
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.2.0

### Description

Angular 22.3.0 fails to resolve its dependency tree in a clean, isolated project when using strict npm peer dependency resolution.

The issue is caused by incompatible dependency requirements between the optional OXC WASM binding and NAPI-RS WASM Runtime.

@angular/build@22.3.0 declares @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.158.0 as an optional dependency.

This binding requires @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime version 2.0.0-alpha.6, while @napi-rs/wasm-runtime@1.2.7 declares peer dependency ranges that do not accept this version.

We reproduced the same issue using four different npm versions: 10.9.9, 10.9.11, 11.21.3, and 12.2.3.

The reproduction does not include application-specific code, custom overrides, or existing node_modules.

Expected behavior: Angular dependencies should resolve successfully without requiring force, legacy-peer-deps, or unsupported dependency overrides.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Create an empty directory.
2. Create the following package.json:

```json
{
  "name": "angular22-isolated-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "@angular/animations": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/common": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/compiler": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/core": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/forms": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/platform-browser": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/router": "22.3.0",
    "rxjs": "7.8.2",
    "zone.js": "0.15.1",
    "tslib": "2.8.1"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@angular/cli": "22.3.0",
    "@angular/compiler-cli": "22.3.0",
    "@angular-devkit/build-angular": "22.3.0",
    "typescript": "6.0.3"
  }
}
```

3. Run the following command:

```bash
npm install --package-lock-only --lockfile-version=3 --strict-peer-deps --legacy-peer-deps=false --force=false --include=optional --include=peer --include=dev --include=prod --ignore-scripts --audit=false --fund=false --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

Expected result: successful dependency resolution and generation of package-lock.json.

Actual result: ERESOLVE, exit code 1, and no package-lock.json generated.

The same result was reproduced using npm 10.9.9, 10.9.11, 11.21.3, and 12.2.3.

### Exception or Error

```text
npm error code ERESOLVE
npm error ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree

npm error While resolving: @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.158.0
npm error Found: @emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.6

npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer @emnapi/core@"^1.7.1 || 2.0.0-beta.2 || 2.0.0-beta.3" from @napi-rs/wasm-runtime@1.2.7

Dependency chain:

@angular-devkit/build-angular@22.3.0
  -> @angular/build@22.3.0
    -> @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.158.0
      -> @emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.6
      -> @napi-rs/wasm-runtime@1.2.7

The required EMNAPI version does not satisfy the WASM Runtime peer dependency range.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Operating System: Windows x64
Node.js: 22.23.5

Tested npm versions:
- 10.9.9
- 10.9.11
- 11.21.3
- 12.2.3

Target Angular version: 22.3.0
Target Angular CLI version: 22.3.0
Target Angular Build version: 22.3.0
TypeScript: 6.0.3
RxJS: 7.8.2
Zone.js: 0.15.1

Registry: https://registry.npmjs.org/

The ng version command cannot be executed using the target project's local Angular CLI because dependency resolution fails before installation completes.
```

### Anything else relevant?

Additional diagnostic findings:

1. Resolving oxc-parser@0.158.0 independently with strict peer dependency resolution succeeds.

2. The standalone OXC lockfile includes native bindings for Windows x64, Linux x64 GNU, and Linux x64 MUSL.

3. The standalone OXC lockfile does not include @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi, @emnapi/core, @emnapi/runtime, or @napi-rs/wasm-runtime.

4. Angular Build 22.3.0 explicitly declares the OXC WASM binding as an optional dependency.

5. Using --omit=optional still reproduces the same ERESOLVE error.

6. Registry metadata inspected on November 27, 2026, shows no published WASM Runtime version within the required ~1.2.7 range that accepts EMNAPI 2.0.0-alpha.6.

Could the Angular CLI team review this optional dependency and provide guidance on an officially supported resolution?

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): bump yargs to 18.2.0
Issues.Body:
Updates `yargs` from `18.0.0` to `18.2.0` on `21.2.x` to align with `main`, deduplicate with `@angular/compiler-cli` and `@angular/localize` (`^18.0.0`), and include the `apply-extends` local prototype pollution fix introduced in `18.1.0` (`AIKIDO-2026-922647`).

Note: Angular CLI does not invoke `yargs.config()`, `yargs.pkgConf()`, or `applyExtends` and does not enable `deep-merge-config`, so `AIKIDO-2026-922647` is not exploitable in `@angular/cli`'s usage.

Closes #34796

### [`v12.23.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.23.0): pnpm 12.23

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.22.0...v12.23.0)

This release adds `pnpm edit`, `pnpm catalog migrate`, and `pnpm link --hard`, and moves deprecation warnings into the install summary. Platform variants are removed, so packages that publish them need to move to `optionalDependencies`. It also carries security fixes: pnpm no longer reads `otp` from config files, and it sends registry credentials only over HTTPS.

##### Minor Changes

##### Packing and publishing

- Removed platform variants. A package version has one archive again.

  pnpm no longer reads `publishConfig.variants` or the `variant` field of `package.json`. `pnpm pack --variant` and the `--upload-variant`, `--variant-integrity` and `--no-variants` options of `pnpm publish` are gone. pnpr no longer accepts variant archives with a version or serves them at `<name>@<version>/variants/<tag>`.

  To ship builds for several platforms, publish each as its own package and list them in `optionalDependencies`. A frozen install of a lockfile that records the variants of a registry package fails with `ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE`. Run `pnpm install` to resolve the lockfile again.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now fail if a package that is not private lists a private workspace package in `dependencies`. A private package is never published, so the published package could not be installed. `devDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, and bundled dependencies are still allowed [#​2321](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2321).

- `pnpm publish` now supports `--new-version <version>`, which sets the version in `package.json` before publishing. With `--recursive`, every selected workspace package is set to the new version [#​2168](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2168).

- `pnpm pack --json` now reports the `package.json` that goes into the tarball, with `publishConfig` and the other publish-time changes applied. Run `pnpm pack --dry-run --json` to preview it without writing a tarball. A dry run still runs `prepack` and `prepare`, unless `--ignore-scripts` is passed.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now add a workspace-root `COPYING` file to a workspace package that has no license file. A `COPYING` file at the package root now counts as the package's license, so the workspace-root `LICENSE` is no longer added next to it.

- Added the `versioning.includePrivatePackages` setting. Set it to `false` to leave private packages out of `pnpm change` [#​13813](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13813).

##### Managing dependencies

- Added the `pnpm edit` command to open an installed package directory in an editor.

- Added `pnpm catalog migrate`, which moves dependency specifiers into the default catalog and replaces them in the workspace projects' `package.json` files with `catalog:`.
